After destroying the Orb of Death, Mel decided to hide into the animal village with Yvette and Ulf. However, she's still denying her magic powers. Never relentess, Edward, ousted of his throne by Lydia, found her and convinced her to go to the Shadowood Academy to control them. But Gwendyal isn't done with the Darkthrop heiress... Mel being in danger, it's up to Stella and Edward to reunite with Galahad and Te'ijal, still bitter about being an human again. However, Nox, that tricked Mel in her previous adventure, is also reappearing, with Uma, a light mage. And Yemite, the little darkling servant, will also join the battle...
Aveyond 3 was fragmented in four chapters. This one is concluding the story and it's still well-written and full of humor: Ulf and Yvette make an appearance though they're not going to join the fight, Mel is still full of sarcasm, Edward is still crushing on her and prompt to go to her rescue, Te'ijal and Galahad are still fighting like the married couple they are and Stella is still the naïve healer. Given the fact that the game is putting you in charge of two different teams (Mel in the Demon Realm and her friends trying to save her in the overworld), you will have new characters joining: Nox and Uma, two mages, a dark one and a light one, that are strongly connected as a Darkling named Yemite, that will be in both teams. Nox and Uma are bickering though are agreeing that they have to help Mel to survive (Nox letting her desire to make sure that Mel will rule the world on the side for her own fate) and Yemite is very happy to serve Mel.
However, while I don't mind the fact that you have two teams, I didn't really enjoyed that fact. I mean; Nox and Uma were really helpful and loosing them made me sad, even for the sake of the story. After that, loosing Galahad and Mel and letting only a team of 3 to conclude the story is also very annoying. Even if well-written, I lost the exciting rush of the two first games, with so many places to visit. Here, the world is kinda small compared.
The game mechanics are still the same and it's the HUD from the Lost Orb that is featured. However, the leveling of spells by fighting and the alchemist feature disappear. Now, you have Edward with a Shard that can be upgraded in Sword Station with some choices to make (as he can also use spells through the sword) and Stella learning a skill by wearing a new staff. They're the ones that are only affected by this new way of playing.
Some quests needs to be done in order to advance in the story, while they're appearing as being a side-quest just for the money. Others are just bonus. But given the fact that you need money to buy stuff, any quest is worthy. You can also spare your money because fast-travel is totally disabled, apart the Reaper, as you need to go to the vampire town.
You can a new pirate ship but you don't have many docks to use. True, in Gates of Nights, you didn't have many islands too. But you had a large  choice of docks, at least for the Mainland. Besides, during the story, you'll acquire a dragon and it will be more useful to use it than the ship itself.
Aveyond comes also with three difficulties: Easy where you're stronger and where most of the enemies don't spawn again after a defeat (yeah, I'm playing in this difficulty), Normal where every is balanced and Hard where you'll die more frequently - though even in Easy, I've been wiped. Well, if a character dies, you can ressucitate them but if your team is wiped, it's game over and it's up to you to load the auto-save (when entering a new screen) or a save of yours.
I'm wondering why I can import my previous save because once launched, Mel lost all her levels, all her gears. It's the same for Edward, it's the same for Stella... and for my gold. So I have played this game for a significant amount of time and I have finally come to the conclusion that I cannot recommend this game right now.
Pros:
So this game is kinda like a visual upgrade for dd1 which I played a lot on the 360 at the time and I enjoyed that game. The maps can have a pretty good learning curve and they can be kinda fun to play on. The gear can be pretty nice to get but later on in the game you will come to find the gear to just be frustrating in terms of the shear amount of rng on the rolls for different stats and so called "passives" which are suppose to give you buffs to certain builds. Then there is the characters. The characters are pretty simple. There are builds for each type of these heros that can make them fun and pretty viable late game(I say this now but Trendy are doing a lot of nerf passes as of late which is kinda why I am kinda done with this game for the time being but more on that later).
Cons:
There are a lot of problems for this game and I feel like the game devs can't use the whole "It's in beta or alpha" argument after the game being out for about 2 going on 3 years now. It is extremly buggy and each update seems to be adding more problems. Then there is the new heroes they have released. You can grind these heroes for this type of currency called "Defender Medals" which can be somewhat easy to grind for if you have a lot of time through the means of daily missions which reset at a wierd time for some in different time zones. There are also weeklys and monthlies but they haven't done a monthly in a good couple of months. Some say it is "pay to win" I like to call it "pay to skip" which is not that bad if you think about it. The gear at later levels can get really frustrating if you don't get the correct rolls. The devs keep just doing the nerf hammer on a lot of heroes and builds people run and barley buffing anything to a viable use. There are massive server issues and bugs that can make the game unplayable for some people for some length of time.
TL:DR This game was a really cool concept and I liked playing it for the time being but it seems the way the devs are doing things at this point in time compared to the time was a payed to get access alpha the devs seemed to have lost sight of what this game was suppose to be. Until the devs either fix the the problems in the game or stop the nerf hammer on a lot of things and buff stuff to be more viable in endgame then I will still not recommend this game.

BEFORE BUYING THIS, PLEASE BUY AVEYOND: LORD OF TWILIGHT, AVEYOND: GATES OF NIGHT, AND AVEYOND: THE LOST ORB, IN THAT ORDER. THIS GAME WILL REVEAL MANY PLOT SPOILERS FOR THE PREVIOUS PARTS AND A COHESIVE STORY CAN ONLY BE FORMED WITH THE PLAYING OF THE OTHER 3 GAMES IN THE SERIES.
Aveyond: The Darkthrop Prophecy is the fourth and final installment in the 4-part series of games that make up Aveyond 3. Don't start with this one, as you'll be missing TONS of backstory. Instead, buy Lord of Twilight first, Gates of Night second, and The Lost Orb third... And finally this one.
Now, I've been following the Aveyond series for several years, back since the first game in 2004 (which doesn't go under the title of "Aveyond", instead; it's called "Ahriman's Prophecy", and it's free from their site,
. I was young, the game was cool, so I stuck with the series. In 2006, the actual Aveyond was released and I was stoked. More of AP? Nice! However, Aveyond 1 was completely different from it's predecessor in the best way possible... Fast forward to today, with me writing this review.
Now, I've had this game for a while. Not on Steam, but from somewhere else, so I've played through it a few times before, so this isn't a "first-time playthrough" review or anything. But without further ado, let's get on to the actual review.
Aveyond: The Darkthrop Prophecy is a great game from a great team of people. It's got a ton of pros... But also it's fair share of cons. I'll list them all out for you, dear reader.
PROS:
+Decent price
+Decent gameplay
+Great story (if you've been following since Lord of Twilight)
+Custom music (not all of the music is build-in RPG Maker music, as one could expect)
+Difficulty selection
+Nostalgia factor (for the select few who played the first Aveyond)
+Combat just works
+Dat plot twist at the end (again, you'll have to have played LoT to understand)
CONS:
-RPG Maker... XP.
Before we go any further, I want to explain why this is a con in detail. Aveyond, the series as a whole, while a great series, is all RPG Maker XP. All of it. From Aveyond 1 (not it's prequel Ahriman's Prophecy, however) to this most current one, Aveyond has been an RPG Maker XP game. After 4 years of making games with RPG Maker XP, you think they'd at least move onto RPG Maker VX Ace (which is what I use), but no. Not even a slight upgrade. Don't get me wrong, there isn't nothing wrong with RPG Maker XP itself (besides its dated-ness) but having a whole series of 7 games be all made in a program that was just barely considered "new" at the time of the first game's release is just baffling.
Now back to the rest of the cons...
-Cannot change screen resolution
-Can be confusing to those who never played any of the other parts of Aveyond 3
-Controls can be awkward
-Moves a bit slow
All in all, I will recommend this game. But please, before you spend $10 on this, buy the others. At least get Lord of Twilight to start you off.

Difficulty for campaign is completely unreasonable.  An example: In one of the GDI missions in Sarajevo, you need to build up a force to attack a heavily fortified Nod position.  It's pretty much impenetrable to ground assaults and air attacks.  You can't use the ion cannon on the main objective because it's shielded.  Now, you would think the logical way to handle this would involve a build up of high-tech, high cost units.  But you can't- because you will be blowing all your money on building and repairing base defenses.  Let your base get destroyed, and you won't be able to complete later objectives.  There are no production facilities you can take out easily to slow down enemy waves.  The only defenses of the Nod base that you can destroy with impunity are the obelisks, which are vulnerable to air assault, but will quickly be rebuilt.
I eventually assaulted the base with ten mammoth tanks, and managed to destroy less than half of it.  I couldn't do more because my base was destroyed at that point.
On all missions, AI will also attack on two or more different fronts, and with such rapid, frequent attacks that even a diehard RTS fan can be overwhelmed.  Also, you can't build walls or gates anymore, because why would anyone want to keep enemy units out of their base easily?  And you can't build in certain locations for no discernible reason, other than the design team said so.
This game is designed to be more frustrating than fun.  It is a far cry from Tiberian Sun.  It's a shame that such a game franchise went in this direction- I'm sure it's a great story, it's got famous actors in it, there are great units...but the fact that missions are designed to screw you over every way possible just makes this not worth the time.

I have always enjoyed the Command & Conquer series. With the exception of 4: Tiberian Twilight, this series has been the granddaddy of RTS games to me, and you'd be hard pressed to make me dislike the series.
C&C 3: Tiberium Wars, as you may have guessed, is the third main entry in the Tiberian Universe. The Global Defense Initiative and the Brotherhood of Nod are at it again in the third world-wide firestorm to occur after the appearance of the deadly crystal, Tiberium. In the perspective of both campaigns, you command forces of the two factions in an effort to dominate the enemy.
Some missions have you build up a base, assemble a strike force, and proceed to take out an objective before your enemy destroys you first. You construct buildings to train/upgrade your forces, and need to divide your attention on taking out the enemy base, while making sure the enemy doesn't destroy yours. In the process, you harvest Tiberium to help fund your genocidal conquest of the map.
Those missions... suck.
However! Some missions give you a limited number of units to strike your foes where it hurts,
. I have a lot more fun with those missions, because I have more fun being given limited forces than maintaining a base while trying to accomplish a hard objective.
The campaign mode shows you a map of "Theatres,"  which each contain a number of missions. Between them, GDI and Nod both have the same number of missions: 17 for each of them, for a total of 34 maps.
When you pick a mission to play, you're given the option of playing on Easy, Normal, or Hard difficulties, with the enemy's units packing more of a punch and being a bit tougher the higher you go. Beating a mission will award you a Bronze, Silver, or Gold Medal, respectively. However, as far as I know, the types of medals you actually earn have no effect on gameplay rewards, so if it's your first time playing, don't feel bad for playing on Easy, 'cuz it's a challenge even then. :avgnmad:
Each mission also has a set of optional bonus objectives; completing them will add a nice little stripe to your medal at the end of a mission. Also, the game has an intelligence database for the two
factions. Getting these entries often requires completing bonus objectives, but destroying a special enemy unit, just playing on, building a special structure, etc. will let you get even more. Getting all intel entries adds another nice completion stripe to your end-of-level medal!
(Now, if you're a story hound like me, this'll let give a lot of interesting stuff to read about the game's world. If not, then there's no shame in missing a couple.)
Even without online functionality, the Skirmish mode is fun, too. Here, you can either team up with friendly AI from the factions and/or pit yourself against opponents, both of which have adjustable difficulty levels. Maps can support 2, 3, 4, 6, or even 8 bases to wage war on each other!
Overall, Tiberium Wars sticks to what worked in the series so far and, while not quite having the same charm as Tiberian Sun, it still stands as a nice game that I wholeheartedly recommend to anyone who likes the genre.

This game is super-fun! There's a lot of really entertaining aspects to the game, from the scenery (gorgeous) to the weapons to the plasmids you use to rebuild your genetic code. Some advice:
-Don't get discouraged with the first big daddy if it's hard to kill. Things get way easier after the first few.
-Pay attention to your surroundings. If there's a big puddle of water, or an oil slick, or a blind corner, use it to your advantage. It will help you. If it’s a logical strategy, it’ll work.
-If you've hypnotized a big daddy, don't shoot it like a retard. It doesn’t understand “I’m sorry please don’t kill me.”
-Don't name hacked security bots. You just get sad when they die.
-Trap bolts = really fun.
-Hack. Everything. You face about a quarter of the enemies that way.

An interesting mod about a forgotten front in WW2, but it could use more polish and balancing. The game represents the conflict between the Imperial Japanese Army (IJA) and the Chinese Army (NRA) during the Second Sino-Japanese War.
Imperial Japanese Army factions:
1. Southern Expeditionary Army- fought in the Pacific and Southeast Asian campaigns. Notable units/call-ins: SNLF marines, Type 1 Ho-ha halftrack, Type 3 Ho-ni tank destroyer, Kongo-class battleship barrage.
2. Central China Army-main Japanese army in China. Notable units: Kwantung Army reinforcements, Ki-48 light bomber, Type 92 Jyu-Sokosha tankette, Type 97 Shinhoto Chi-ha medium tank.
3. China Garrison Army – also called the Kwantung Army based in Manchukuo.  Notable units/call-ins: Zero fighter strafe, Type 89B Chi-ro medium tank, Sector artillery, Unit 731 mortar squad.
Chinese Army factions:
1. National United Front- this is the alliance between the Kuomintang and the Communists  (the latter, later known as the People’s Liberation Army or PLA). Notable units: Eight Route Army guerrillas, Type 1 AT gun, Type 92 field gun, Renault FT-17 light tank.
2. Chinese Expeditionary Force- represents the Western Allies-supplied and trained X and Y Force. Notable units: M4A3 Sherman medium tank, M3 Stuart light tank, British-equipped squad.
3. Elite German Armed Division – represents the divisions trained by Generaloberst Hans von Seeckt’s military missions to China.  Notable units: Panzer I light tank, Pak36 AT gun, sFH 18 field gun, T-26 light tank.
Positives:
+Except for the tanks and vehicles, units are detailed and accurate. It’s a bit weird to see Chinese infantry sporting the Stahlhelm (German helmet), but it’s historically accurate.  The Chinese Army was at one point or another trained and supplied by Germany, Russia, US and UK.
+Equipment and weapons used by both sides are fairly represented across all of the available armies or doctrines for each side.
+Extensive unit variety.
+Infantry-oriented combat.
+Armored battles are fairly light tank affairs so flanking and maneuver are emphasized.  The Sherman is like a Tiger II in this game.
+Music from “The Last Samurai”
+Donkey bombs and Kamikaze units.  Wasteful, but gets the job done.
Negatives:
-Graphics and sound glitches abound.  Also, models tend to disappear when zooming out.
-Mortars and artillery are terribly overpowered in this game. They are laser-like in precision and squad wipes are common.
-AI is broken on some maps, even on the mod-exclusive ones.  It tends to camp an area doing nothing.
-Units are prohibitively expensive.  Considering both sides suffered more than a million casualties in this conflict, infantry should have lower manpower and pop cost.
-As mentioned vehicles look bland and drab.  Some of the camo patterns are incorrect.  It would help to show the elaborate markings and insignia of the IJA tank regiments.
-Retains the base game’s unit voice clips.
-Weakness of the base game is carried over like less than optimal unit pathing and AI.
Overall, this mod is the weakest among the available mods for Company of Heroes on Steam.  The other two, The Great War and Europe at War are better, in my opinion.  Nevertheless, it provides a fresh game experience for CoH fans.

For someone unfamailair with the franchise; it's a turnbased, tactical, quasi-football simulation with rpg and progression mechanics using the warhammer universe.  Kind of a mouthful right?  It works suprisingly well though.
This game is almost less of a sequal than a graphics and UI overhaul of the first game.  The game itself is functionally identical in terms of gameplay, but all the peripheral portions have been improved.  The UI is now easy to use and mostly intuitive (if you assume that should just be a given, play the first game and weep).  The graphics are not just functional as they were in the original, but actually quite good with cutscenes showing the action and giving a visceral thrill when your minotaur curb stomps a dwarf.  Full game pad support.  The team manager has more depth and it's now easy to almost instantly create custom leagues to play in.  You also now have the ability to trade your players online to other people which is just an interesting feature.
One of the largest improvements is the addition of an actual tutorial in the form of the campaign.  It's a little slow but actually tells you what does what as opposed to the original blood bowls method of, "Just click around and hope for the best."  The campaigns narrative is also charmingly silly which is a plus.
Given the longevity of the previous game the community is going to be extremely active for some time as well, so that's another bonus.
Now this is not a game for everyone.  Like any authentic adaptation of a games workshop title, die rolls are king and you will inevitably end up cursing at your screen as what should have been a sure thing somehow turns into disaster.  If you've never called the RNG a ♥♥♥♥ing cheater, then you haven't actually played a games workshop title.  With that said though, the opposite can occasionally happen too, and it feels amazing.
The only real downside is that the previous incarnation of blood bowl had 23 races, this has 8 (and doesn't have the undead, which was my favorite you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s!)  The difference will be made up in DLC's which, depending on your preference is either fine or, to use the the langauge of the forum screamers, a bloodsucking scam that even EA would be ashamed of.  Personally I'm ok with it, and would rather have the game right now to play than wait however long it would be to get all the other races out simultaneously, but it nevertheless IS a negative.  This is a Null issue to new comers to the game but blood bowl 1 vets will probably feel like thier choices have been severely cut back.
On the whole it's a pretty game that is silly fun and a lot more welcoming to new players than the first.  Buy it, Play it, cripple a scaven and laugh.  It's good times.  8/10

I have been a fan of the "Tales of" games ever since i played Tales of Symphonia on the GameCube. I have probably played this game more than any other person with 600+ hours. This review may cantian spoilers.
Lets first review the story.
The Story is the basic hero gains power to confront the evil Lord of Calamity. The story is linear in the respect that you can't choose dialouge or how the game progresses. However, this doesn't detract from the story. You can do side quests to learn more about certain charateters and why they are the way they are or about the world in general. I enjoy learning about the world created in the a game and this allows you to do that if you so choose.
Lets review the (playable) characters.
The characters are likable with Sorey being the main protagonist. Sorey was raised by a community of seraphim along with his friend Mikleo. Their interactions are like any best friend interactions are some funny and some serious. It was fun to see how these character deveolped over the course of the game.
Lailah is the seraph that Sorey makes a pact with to get his purification powers to face the Lord of Calamity.  She is "guiding light" directing the other party members to seek out their own answers to issues presented to the party members.
Edna is seraph who like teasing Mikleo to no end. She is my favorite because of the comedy relief she adds to the group dynamic.
Alisha is the princess of the Kingdom of Hyland. She is deterimened person to do what she feels is right even if  it isn't the easy path.
Dezel is a seraph that accompanies Rose around and protects her. He is a lonely and deterimed seraph will do anything in pursuit of his task.
Rose is the leader of the Sparrowfeathers. She has a strong sense of justice and lets other know how she feels on issues.
Zaveid is a flanboyant seraph that pursuse his own goals the way he wants, but when he joins teh party he has a surprising brotherly side.
The characters did develope over the course of the game and seeing the interactions is an enjoyable part of the game.
Now lets review the leveling and battle system.
The fisrt thing is that leveling in this game isn't as important has your equipment. The fusing system for weapons and accessories does take time understand and master. However, it allows you to create sets of equipment that you can use to overcome any foe.
Also as you level up, you level up your titles which provide different benifits for each character.
Some say that battle feels like button mashing and it certainly can feel that way, but the battle system is much more subtle than that.
In battle certian characters have certain types of attacks form martial, hidden, or seraphic artes. characters either have martial and hidden atres or martial and seraphic artes. Later in the game you get the ability to armatize which has hidden and seraphic artes. Each arte has a damage type along with an effect or two, so understanding your enemy strength weaknesses willl help you greatly in battle. However one doesn't need to spend time memorizing each artre and what it can, i certainly didn't, but when facing a powerful foe reviewing artes and changing equipment really helps.
There was only one thing i disliked about this game and that was that the human characters always in battle and you can't switch them out.
I would recommend this game to any person how likes RPGs.

OOOOOOOOH boy where do I start
Ok so I have been following this game's development since around 2015 when it was in its earliest stages of development and I can honestly say without any doubt in my mind that A Hat in Time lives up to the expectations the developers (Gears for Breakfast) and We, the fans have built up.
This game is a lovely 3D collectathon platformer that harkens back to the olden glory days of mascot based Collectathon 3D Platformers in the Nintendo 64, GameCube, Playstation and Dreamcast days.
It is not just a throwback though as this game has SEVERAL unique features that other games in the same vain do not, Take the focus on hats for example. The default hat is very boring and only points you to where you need to go, but once you get that sprint visor you know you are in for a true ride. The focus on different abilities unlocked through different hats is for what I say is just simply cool.
This game also DECIMATES Yooka-Laylee (another 3D collectathon indie platformer) and takes all the ideas and concepts which that game should have had, and increases them and expands upon them tenfold (just check the Yooka-Laylee reviews)
AND THE ART STYLE DUDE its so beautiful. It may not be the most graphically impressive art style ever to exist, but it looks DAMN good and everything looks so absolutely cartoony, fun, bright and childish, it just adds this charm to an already charming game that will have it age wonderfully.
All I can say is this is one of the most remarkable 3D platformers I have played in the past decade and this is a MUST BUY for anyone who grew up in the late 90s and early 2000s or to anyone who just simply wants to have a fun game to play

I love Blood Bowl... (actually any GW small combat/skirmish game to be fair..) and have been playing it since I picked up the tabletop game over 15 years ago
My Opinion:
the Pros-
Graphics: Awesome step (read leap) up from BB1
Teams: love the addition of the Bretonnians and the other teams look great
Team Creation: easy to use and the auto fill is a nice addition for hassel free setup for those just wanting to play.
Gameplay: Solo play the AI feels more refined than BB1 and the match-up system is much better
"Campaign" / "Story mode" / "Tutorial": Although boring for seasoned players it isn't to bad for new coaches
the Cons-
Animations: Repetative
Camera: is anoying. You have replaced action and excitement with camera tricks that get boring...
Solo Play: Although it is there it doesn't have the same feel that the bb1 Campaign had.. bb1 gave me a feeling of taking a team of greenhorns from new to world champs.. Solo in BB2 misses this completely as there is no real feeling of ladder progression.
Things it still needs: (In my opinion)
- Camera Rotation
- Grid for player movement
- More race/role specific animations
- A more story focused solo game that isn't based around the Reavers
- More Teams, I know it will come.. just dont skimp on the number and bring back all the teams from BBCE.. I want my Chaos Dwarfs in HD  :)
- Freedom of choice on the Team colours and More Heads for players. (see below)
I do feel that from BB1 you have made a step in the right direction for team visual creation
however...
Bloodbowl in essence is a game based on plastic models/figures. 50% of the game is about creating your own teams identity.. Painting them.. Basing them.. Giving them names.. creating their history/story and overall building a personalised identity for them to the point that when playing you cheer when they succeed and feel pain when your best player has a crippling injury.
To me this is what makes the GW games like Bloodbowl, Mordheim and Necromunda such great games..
Even with the limitation on available models for the TTop version you would go that extra mile to make each player individual in their own way..
I understand the need for limitations on molded models but I do not understand the need to have limitations in a graphical based game...
Even just allowing us to change hair colour and add/remove beards/Facial accessories would be good..
Freedom to change colours on the Armour rather than forcing us to use a limited range of preset schemes which sadly lack imagination as all teams have a similar set..
And yes it is more man hours to provide these options to your customers but it is also the difference between hitting the bullseye or just missing again on your 4th attempt...
Overall I would say 7/10 Touchdowns

Lets review blood and bacon. My reviews follow a pro/ con style and i will try to be as detailed as i can.
Pro:
Its a cheap game. Seriously its only $1 so no need for high expectations of graphics or gameplay. It is simple and fun.
Loads of gameplay and easter eggs. You play from day 1 to day 101 killing pigs with a small variety of side arms and primary guns. Easter eggs that this games provides are to a degree well hidden and enjoyable to experience.
Great time waster. It is a simple game that you can play in your off time in small bursts while waiting for another game to install. Playing it too long might make you fee bored so thats why i reccomend the game in small bursts.
Con:
The gun choices are very small and lacks much variety. You have shotguns, assult rifles, rpg, and handgun. I would like to see more guns in a variety of types like add snipers, lmg, or machine pistols. (This is a nitpick)
Some easter eggs are very well hidden by which i mean the keys. Some are only reachable when in free roam mode and under the map or inside a building that the player can not get in. (This is a nitpick)
Recycle the bosses. You will fight the same big pig that ♥♥♥♥♥ and pukes on the player every day that is divisable by 20. The boss is not very interesting and fighting the boss on day 20 compaired to day 80 is no difference. (This is a nitpick)
The jokes or whenever the farmer tends to talk is pretty cring worthy. His dialog is not entertaining after you hear the same dialog in later days. It was kinda funny at first but then becomes very tiresome. (This is a nitpick)
There is no music during the day. It is very annoying to be killing pigs and not having some type of music playing during these times. Sure you wouldnt want to have just one song available to play for all the days but having music makes the game a tad more interesting. (This is a nitpick)
Conclusion:
Blood and bacon is one of those good games to play when you have spare time to kill and it is very cheap so it is impressive how enjoyable a simple $1 game is. I do want to see more add ons to the game and more achievements to do but that is something we will have to wait and see based on what the dev decides to do.

Rising Storm is a standalone expansion pack to Red Orchestra 2, an online, first person, war world 2 shooter. Red Orchestra 2 featured battles on the eastern front of WWII, Rising Storm changes the scenery and focuses on the pacific theatre of war.
Teamwork is crucial, and it really makes the game something special. Rising Storm is not a game that encourages Rambo's or lone wolfs. If you try to be the hero and run off on your own, you are going to be killed.
The team based game-play provides experiences and intense action that just isn't found in other titles. There is nothing like the feeling of pulling off a full team banzai run to capture a point with 32 of your teammates The game's sound is amazing with everyone screaming BBAANNNZAAIIII as gun fire screams by your head and your friend is blown into bits by an artillery shell. Tripwire really deserves credit for the sound in this game, everything sounds amazing! With a nice headset, or a good sound system, this game will blow you away.
Don't get me wrong, I love this game, but the graphics don't even come close to competing with the completion, such as graphically impressive Battlefield, or even the somewhat dated Call of Duty engine. The graphics, at best, are adequate. If graphics are important for your experience, you may want to consider skipping this title.
Your ping is going to be ugly as well. Throughout my games I've noticed my average ping to be about four times higher then a game of Team Fortress 2 or Counter Strike GO. The strange thing is, I haven't found it to impact the game-play much. Either the game's net-code is constructed to handle high ping, or I'm personally not sensitive to it.
With the realistic sound, and the horrors of war occurring all around you, this is not a game to play if your looking for a relaxing experience. Most of the populated servers are well administrated, which encourage balanced teams, which lead to close intense matches for the majority of games I've played.
The game features the usual classes such as rifleman, assault, sniper, etc, and contains a large amount historic American and Japanese weapons. New to rising storm is the flamethrower class for the Americans and the Mortar class for the Japanese. I personally found the flamethrower hard to use, but in the hand of a skilled player, it is great at clearing out choke-points and buildings. I found the mortar much easier to use and it is great at spamming explosives down range at bottlenecks on the map the Americans are trying to push through.
The game community is not large, and with the small player-base, the player community tend to be enthusiasts and provide good team based games. On the downside, as a new player, playing against these experienced players, you are going to die... a lot. As a newb, it will be frustrating as hell, but if you stick with it, you will start to learn how to play, and the game will reward you for being patient.
So... should I buy it?
As mentioned above, the game has a few problems, the graphics could be better, the difficulty can be very unforgiving, and the small player-base can make finding/joining good servers difficult. If you can look past these flaws, you won't find a better shooter, period. The guns are amazing, the game-play is great, and the sound is epic. I can easily recommend this title at its current full price. If the flaws cause you to be concerned, wait for a sale, and pick it up cheap. I promise you that you won't be sorry you did.

This game is a pretty middle-of-the-road, if entertaining (in an arcade rail-shooter kind of way) third-person space shooter.    I do think the comparisons to Starfox, Panzer Dragoon etc. are just a bit hyperbolic - the game is really only superficially similar to these well-regarded classics. It is ultimately more like a third-person Galaga/Asteroids clones with a few Starfox elements like the tunnel level etc. The graphics and sound are fine, if not technically/artistically impressive, and the controls of the various pilotable spacecraft are very responsive using a X-Box 360 controller.
There are several different level types, from needing to destroy a certain number of objects/enemies before the timer runs out, surviving an onslaught of obstacles for a certain amount of time to navigating tunnels, and these tend to repeat with the odd boss-battle ad-nauseum. As I've not invested very much time in the game at this time, I can't comment on later levels.
All in all, it's not a bad little arcadey game for 24 cents (the price I paid during a sale), and I've certainly dropped a quarter into far worse arcade machines for a single play, but I would say that it's definitely a harder sell at above $1 or so. At the right price, it's a simple little arcade game that scratches that certain itch in small bursts, but it's not something I can see myself investing a lot of time in.

The top-rated helpful review compares this game positively to 3D shmups like Star Fox and urges the reader to purchase this game immediately if they enjoy the others. Don't do that.
Since the comparison to Star Fox has already been made, I'm going to roll with it. We're going to be focusing on the similarities and differences between this game and Star Fox 64, which might seem unfair once I get into it, but 64 is eighteen years old and this game came out this year.
First off, the flying. Your ship (no matter which one you select,) has no real weight to it. It floats gleefully around the screen with such speed that it highlights more especially than anything the stirring lack of actual control you have over it and the lack of any real animation to it. The ship floats where you point it and that's it. No maneuvering, no complexity of control, and no real animation to the motion besides a slight tilt in the direction you're heading.
Okay, the flying's not great, but 3D shmups are more about the shooting anyway. Star Fox 64 had satisfyingly fast shooting with incrimental power upgrades for your lasers. This game SORT OF has a similar upgrade, but it is automatically collected - no challenge there - and only serves to slightly speed up your INCREDIBLY SLOW AND INACCURATE SHOOTING. Your shots don't arc based on motion or follow the angle of your ship, they go forward on a fixed line, meaning you need to line up perfectly with your enemy to shoot them. This would be a small flaw if your ship didn't block most of the screen and make actually seeing and lining up with an enemy an incredibly difficult effort that ultimately only serves to crash your ship into the target and not actually give any meaningful award or feedback for shooting the target down.
The screen is locked exactly as it is, so your range of motion is incredibly limited. This wouldn't be an issue considering the complete LACK OF DIFFICULTY for most of the game, but sooner rather than later, enemies and their attacks start tracking you. With the screen locked as it is and your ship as floaty and unresponsive as it is, you very quickly start losing life to attacks you've got almost no chance of escaping. This is what we call ARTIFICIAL DIFFICULTY. It's when a stupidly easy game makes a stupid and hamfisted attempt to make itself not so stupidly easy.
There's little to no variety in the levels. Honestly, the major difference between one level and the next is what enemy or threat you're meant to be shooting or avoiding. There's briefly an in-door segment with metal walls to avoid, but it's not contextualized as a huge enemy ship or planet or base or anything, and once it's done you're back to the completely linear space hallway.
The visual style is incredibly lazy. Nothing looks interesting or memorable in any way, and the utter lack of animation beyond direct motion kills any sort of interest the bland designs and lazy attacks might generate.
I'd like to say there's something positive to this game to help redeem it or maybe make it more aggrieving that the rest is so lazy and boring, but there isn't.
I can't put in the effort to be mad at a game that didn't have any effort put into at all.
TL;DR Slow, boring, lazy, ugly, and uninpsired. No matter what other games you enjoy, pass this one up. It's not worth your time, let alone your money.

I had been putting this game off for a while and since it was on sale, I decided to just go for it and get it, despite the negative reviews revolving the main character which I unfortunately have to agree with now,
Aesthetically, this game is very pretty. The horror elements were quirky and it had style, although it wasn't particularly frightening.
Gameplay-wise, it may as well play itself. The puzzles were pretty easy, you're not left there figuring out what to do. However, there was a part in Act 3 where you have to repeat the whole segment over and over again - amounting to about four times...? All for the purpose of just small differences in between. The repetitiveness in that part was honestly just annoying and it would have been better if they just extended Act 3 rather than making you play it several times. I was enjoying the game up until Act 3, which was frustrating and just boring if I'm honest.
I was hoping the ending would make up for it. It didn't. Not only did it not answer any questions, but it just confused me even more. You're given no answers and then it's over.
It could have been better if the main character had more... character? She's so UNRESPONSIVE to everything. She doesn't have any reaction to the weird things she encounters, all you can get out of her really is just '...' Literally.
I mean, if the point of the story is that it's open to interpretation, I get that, but combining the fact that the character is so deadpan and that the ending gives you no answers (you don't have much to speculate really), you don't get any satisfaction from completing the game.
TL;DR: short and kinda sweet game (until Act 3). It's pretty, but ultimately boring and dissapointing due to the main character's lack of character and bad ending.

Stray Cat Crossing is a niche game targeted at fans of RPG Maker cult games such as The Witch's House, Ib, OFF and Ao Oni.
The art and visual design is perfectly executed throughout the entire game; it's probably some of the best art you'll see in an RPG Maker project. However, it lacks substance in the crucial areas which made those games so memorable: story and originality. The writing is poorly executed and, although the game is rife with metaphorical imagery, none of it feels really meaningful. The beautifully rendered characters are not compelling or developed in interesting ways which make you care about them. As a fan of these types of games, I personally enjoyed Stray Cat Crossing for its art and not much else, and I feel that ultimately it was a bland experience.

The first and most welcome change is its open world. Zestiria removes the pen that once confined us to narrow corridors of trees and bushes and lets you freely journey through a nice variety of locations that include green pastures, sand-swept deserts, and gloomy swamps. This gives Zestiria’s world a sense of immersion that some of its more linear predecessors lack. Treasure chests and stat-boosting herbs found throughout a typical Tales world are still there, but I like that Zestiria also includes Normin: cute little critters tucked away in  hidden corners that grant special skills to equipment. There are also Lords of the Land, helpful deities that let you do things like fast-travel and replenish treasure chests if you establish a good enough rapport with them. These are all nice rewards for putting on your wide-brimmed fedora and venturing through the landscape.

OOOOOOOOH boy where do I start
Ok so I have been following this game's development since around 2015 when it was in its earliest stages of development and I can honestly say without any doubt in my mind that A Hat in Time lives up to the expectations the developers (Gears for Breakfast) and We, the fans have built up.
This game is a lovely 3D collectathon platformer that harkens back to the olden glory days of mascot based Collectathon 3D Platformers in the Nintendo 64, GameCube, Playstation and Dreamcast days.
It is not just a throwback though as this game has SEVERAL unique features that other games in the same vain do not, Take the focus on hats for example. The default hat is very boring and only points you to where you need to go, but once you get that sprint visor you know you are in for a true ride. The focus on different abilities unlocked through different hats is for what I say is just simply cool.
This game also DECIMATES Yooka-Laylee (another 3D collectathon indie platformer) and takes all the ideas and concepts which that game should have had, and increases them and expands upon them tenfold (just check the Yooka-Laylee reviews)
AND THE ART STYLE DUDE its so beautiful. It may not be the most graphically impressive art style ever to exist, but it looks DAMN good and everything looks so absolutely cartoony, fun, bright and childish, it just adds this charm to an already charming game that will have it age wonderfully.
All I can say is this is one of the most remarkable 3D platformers I have played in the past decade and this is a MUST BUY for anyone who grew up in the late 90s and early 2000s or to anyone who just simply wants to have a fun game to play

Red Orchestra, the original, was extremely good. The sequel, Heroes of Stalingrad, is equally fantastic. The squad-based Infantry combat is very quick paced, with short times between respawns, helping keep the flow of action. The only thing, for me, that lets this game down is the♥♥♥♥♥♥poor job they did of the Armoured Vehicles. You get 2 tanks: the T34 for the Ruskis, and the Pz4 for the German lads. Tank combat in the original was awesome, with different armoured vehicles and variants of each, using different shell types to try and kill the enemy tanks before you were killed yourself. In RO2, tank combat works like this: Two tanks spot eachother, they take turns firing shells. It takes 3 good hits to kill one of them, so if you started firing first and hit the first shot, then you'll probably win that fight. The maps that force you to play Armour crews are tedious and awful. Those that mix the tank in with a load of infantry work really well, because the tank is there to be an absolute beast in support of the men, terrifying the enemy.
Play this ♥♥♥♥ing game for the high-octane, adrenaline fuelled infantry combat. It rocks hard. Don't♥♥♥♥♥♥around with the armoured stuff, it'll leave you disappointed.

Command & Conquer 3: Tiberium Wars keeps to the roots of the C&C genre in terms of base building, unit construction, and faction diversity. Minor changes are resource generation (Pre determined pools of tiberium exist), the special abilities of the factions, and trying to keep your enemy from unit swarming you (good luck with that haha). This is possibly the last true C&C game to come from EA that retains much of the C&C core (don't get me wrong, the Red Alert, Generals, and Kane's Wrath timelines are fun to play as well, not to mention KW is a throwback to Tiberian Sun in a manner). C&C 3 is also fun because you actually get to duke it out in diverse areas and SOME important cities all around the globe.
I strongly recommend this game to any 90's kid.

This is not like Star Fox! After buying this game, I was looking forward to what I thought was the PC's answer to Star Fox. I also didn't see a proper sequel to the Star Fox series coming anytime soon. I doubt that Star Fox Zero (the upcoming one for the Wii U; not sure if that's the exact title) will offer much either.
Suffice it to say, I was very disappointed in this. But I suppose there are a few pros. Here's the breakdown:
PROS
+ Cool textures for the price (I payed $0.24 for it instead of the original $5 price)
+ Music is okay and works for the game
CONS
- Levels are generic and repetitive. Environments are quite static. I had to double check this page to see if it was EA (Early Access), but it wasn't, and to be fair, even in EA, games usually have more to them. The space levels are the most generic; you either have a static background and a "starfield" whose simplistic particles keep coming towards you monotonously, or you have a planet under you that appears to be a scrolling surface. In short, this is an inferior Star Fox that borrows from its worst parts.
- Graphics settings are minimal, consisting only of resolution and a fullscreen toggle.
- Checkpoints are thrown at you at the end of boss fights that seem to occur every 4 levels, and you only have 1 life, so if you die during the boss fight, you have to repeat those 4 levels, which is frustrating when you beat some of the more challenging levels.
- Powerups don't seem to change anything except for the appearance of your ammo being fired. The purple stuff in your final weapon upgrade wiggles left and right in its trajectory which may slightly increase the radius making it more likely to collide with enemy hitboxes, but not enough to be worth the effort. If you get enough powerups without getting hit too much, you get a shield, but I can't remember if it absorbs 1 damage before collapsing or if it even does that much.
- No option to use the mouse to move the ship or to even remap keybindings.
CONCLUSION
Don't waste your time, energy, or money on this. It's not worth it. There are far better FREE games out there. I am going to ask for a refund (it sounds like a lot of trouble for $0.24, but they shouldn't be able to profit from this). This game is one way to pass the time, but I know of a better way, go play Solitaire! Sun Blast is not nearly as fun as Star Fox, so don't be fooled.

Have you ever romantically thought about the experience of living in a lonely wooden cabin, far from the civilization, in the icy north of canada? Can you imagine this ambivalent mood, being in a beautiful, but also hazardous wild nature. Do you want to feel the pulse of the wilderness to experience your own limits? This is the atmosphere, the game is build around. It's not about fear or depression - it's about living at the limits and the willpower to survive.
The game achieves this by a very unique and own game art, realistic game mechanics and the beautiful northern setting with stunning varying light based on weather and day-night cycle. The realism of the game adds more depths to the decisions you make. There is rarely a strict pattern or some kind of "best practice", that you can follow - it's truely up to you, to decide if a risk is worth the reward. Even your bad decisions may bring you an exciting experience. You will die often in the beginning. But everytime you start a new game, you will be enriched by this experience, getting a feeling for the dangers out there and how to withstand them.
Still unsure? Check this points:
You like to play in an open ended scenario, with no other goal, than to survive? If not, than better wait until the storymode is added.
Bad experience with Early Access Games? This title is nearly bugfree and in a steady development by a small, but professional and experienced gamestudio.
Does the current content justify the pricing? In my opinion it is more than enough and there are regular content updates, delivered mostly polished and bugfree. It's really high quality entertainment for an unbeatable low price.
To come to an end.. If you like this genre in general you will not regret the purchase. Have fun and a lucky hunt :P

Wow. The Long Dark.
First off, I must say that this game isn't for everyone. With Story Mode unavailable in Alpha, a death means instant restart. This can be frustrating, especially when fighting wolves (I can't for the life of me figure out a good way to do this, especially when I can't find a knife). And if you want an FPS style survival, that's not this game. It's first person, but the only gun, a slow firing hunters rifle, is extremely rare; I've only found it twice.
That being said, I didn't expect to love this game. I generally play FPS or action games like Destiny, Call of Duty, and Assassin's Creed. I actually saw this game in Game Informer magazine and it just looked really interesting. Regardless, I do love this game. I don't have a lot of Steam games (I play Xbox One mostly) but this is by far my favorite one.
So what's so great about this game? Well, like I said before, it is pretty frustrating. This means that when you get some decent gear, properly time your actions, and start exploring strong- it feels very rewarding. Also, there are only five other mammals you run into. These are dead humans, wolves, bears (I've not yet seen one), and rabbits. There is also ice fishing. Having just a few AI means a quiet and calm feeling of isolation, even though I play on Voyageur mode (normal) not Pilgrim (easy/peaceful). The beautiful isolation combined with the slightly cartoonish graphics and landscape make for a stunning game. I play on Low graphics and it still looks beautiful; my only problem is black lighting indoors, which is my laptops fault.
Get this game. If you want to wait to get it on sale, sure. I waited a couple weeks and got it at $12 instead of $20, but that was recently so it might not go on sale again for a while. Regardless, it is definitely worth $20 USD. Get it if you can handle the quirks I mentioned in the beginning.

A short horror game made with RPG Maker. Come to think of it, it's kinda weird that this engine was originally made for RPGs, but that most of the best games made with it are horror adventure games.
Although the beginning feels very horror-ish (red screen tones, jump scares, you get the idea), as the game progresses and you learn more about the plot, the horror elements get less frequent the game gets more surreal.
+ The pixel art is great, from environments to sprites and characters portraits. The music is also pretty good. It's rare to hear post-rock in video games.
+ It manages to tell an interesting story in a couple of hours, while still leaving a bit open to interpretation. The characters are very unique (particularly the Japanese goat-mom-witch).
+ / - The gameplay is pretty standard for this kind of game (mostly puzzles, and one chase sequence). The last part can feel a bit repetitive since it involves some kind of sequence loop (I love this kind of stuff, but apparently I'm the only one who does).

Wow! An emphatic recommendation from me.
Let's get the negatives out of the way first -- it's short, it has some issues with crashes (they don't stop you from completing the game), and gameplay is limited to fetching things and chatting with things, with attempts to add variety missing the mark.
For another game those might be dealbreakers, but Stray Cat Crossing isn't about the mechanics. It's about the spooky world and demented characters which have sprung from the minds of its creators, and in every way that it needs to immerse you in that world, it succeeds.
The soundtrack is good -- each track is short, tight, distinct, and enhances the game's atmosphere.
The plot has its fair share of memorable moments. It's convoluted but considering the nature of the world we are visiting, maybe that's just what it should be. It has inspired numerous theories and speculation among fans.
But the artwork, Wow, this is some of the best pixel art I've seen in years. It approaches the level of the top titles of the 16 bit era. Comparisons with Chrono Trigger come to mind, which is simply astounding considering the dream team behind the art of CT!
And we can't overlook the price, which is only a few bucks on Steam at the time of writing, so it's hard to say you aren't getting value for money.
Above all I think it's the character concepts which make this game a must play. It's rare to come across characters this weird, creepy and creative in any title of any budget. Stray Cat Crossing ultimately serves as a showcase for the eclectic imaginations of its authors, and in this regard it's a complete and unique success.
The other comparison I couldn't help making was to the Wadjet Eye P&C titles I've been playing recently, some of which are real works of art. If Jurlo and JetPackGone polished the weak points in their output and produced a full-length adventure game with a surreal horror atmosphere reminiscent of Stray Cat's, we could be looking at a one-of-a-kind masterpiece.
If summary if you have a little nostalgia for the heydays of 16 bit RPGs or adventure games, and you're into creepy atmospheric horror, and you won't rage when the game occasionally crashes or shows a rough edge, Stray Cat is a must play.

Disturbed is a Free2play adventure indie game with a dark but cool art style. It is single player and rather casual, as it only takes around one hour to complete with all achievements.
Story
Disturbed throws you in a World which fades into darkness. You are a farmer, trying to find out where the disease that corrupts the land comes from, so you leave your farm and head out. Overall a good story as the World really drags you into it. I did not identify with the character, even though I was making all choices for him.
Gameplay
The gameplay of Disturbed is rather old-school. You get a nicely drawn picture, some text, describing what happened and some choices to make. Often a choice will kill you and you will have to reload a save and choose the other option, but you will get an achievement every time you die because of something else, also was I curious how exactly I was going to die, so I died plenty of times. Do not fear that you will have to read, as it is not described to briefly, but sufficient. Per Place you go to you will not have to read anything bigger than this paragraph.
Graphics
Well Graphics… The game did not have the usual graphics, neither did it have any animations, but this is part of the experience and why this is this unique. As already said all you get are pictures, but even a potato could run the game.
Do I Recommend?
Yes. The game is short and may be boring if you do not like games of this type, but look through the screenshots up above in the description you should give it a try, as it is for free and fast to download. I enjoyed it.

But i hear you saying why the negative review? Surely this is an amazing game that you can blow countless hours at and feel constant rewards and satisfaction, well yes it is at first. After 3 days of this Power Up Update the nerf bats came in strong, nerfing new content that made the original 4 characters viable in Nightmare IV Difficulty, You would still get one shot and had to have the best gear available to stand a chance but now without your dps you then have to rely on your towers. Nightmare IV is by design isn't meant to be doable with the original 4 characters regardless of gear or skill level.

I've been a fan of the "Tales of" series for a long time and I want to like them all, but I don't. This is one of them.
It was a combination of little things that made me stop playing this game. First was the story. It was bland. It was the same "you are the chosen hero" type thing, but I was okay with that since there's more to this game than the story. So how's the gameplay?
When it comes to battle, I feel like Bamco has never really been able to hit the sweet spot ever since it switched to a full 3D combat style. Cameras are all over the place and the fighting was very unrewarding. After 10 hours in, I still felt like I was button mashing with no regards to what's going on. There's this mechanic where characters fuse together essentially become one. So instead of having four players fighting, you're down to 2. In my opinion, a good Tales of  game would incorporate all the characters to produce combos. A quick example: a mage would cast a spellbinding magic while the swordsman attacks.
Instead, you have two overly busy looking character spinning around with magic fire swords while another is throwing water dragons. It's flashy, but you have no idea what's going on. Seriously, just go back to the basics of HP/MP and throw away the gimmicky stuff.
The one thing this game probably has for them is the characters. They're quite likeable and none of them are annoying. Character designs are great. The story focus on war so it's a bit more mature which is great unlike a certain other game that theme was "friendship" (cough Graces f cough).
Overall, I don't recommend unless you're a Tales of fan, but even then, I don't recommend it.
In case you're wondering, my favourite Tales of game is Symphonia. It's also a "Chosen Hero" story, but the theme is very complex with racism, religion, slavery, and war. The twist in the end is pretty good too. Also, the combat is before the full 3D transition, so it's classic 'Tales of' combat.

I've known about a Hat in Time for maybe a few months, thinking it looked like a decent platformer, and that I would check it out as I'm a fan of the genre.  The last actual platformer I played (off the top of my head) is Super Mario Galaxy 2.  Going in with little to no expectations, I was given something else entirely than what I expected.  This game grabbed me from the get go, from it's colorful and bright setting/art, to the fluid animations and controls, and dare I say, how god damn adorable it is.  Everything about it, the level design, the platforming, collecting items, the hats, just everything oozes charm, and a passion for this forgotten genre.  And the music is one of the best OSTs I've heard.  The more you play, the more it ramps up in terms of quality.
Of course there are flaws, but the shear quality, thought, and passion put into a Hat in Time completely overshadows those flaws.  It's a little too easy, the geometry of the levels can mess with you a little bit, some bugs.  But I consider these mere nitpicks rather than actual flaws of this otherwise fantastic game.
In short, I love this game.  It completely took me by surpise and blew me away.  I had an absolute blast from start to end, its just pure fun.  I know there is mod support and new chapters/levels coming in the future, but I sincerely hope Gears for Breakfast considers a sequel.  If you are fan of platformers or just like games that are just fun, I cannot recommend this game enough.

A Wii game that hits late the PC scene and one that tries to sell itself as a Starfox, Space Harrier type of flying game.  Wii roots can be seen right away on the loading screen where the player is recommended to keep the wrist strap on at all time. Now just how many play this with a remote like on the Wii?
So is it any good? Well yes with some caveats:
Pro's:
+ Pricing
+ Simple gameplay - Pick it up and off you go.  There is even an autofire so you dont need to mash fire button.
+ Challenge. Simple to learn but achievement stats speak for themselves: Those gold medals are tough.
+ Content and variation. Yes it's listed below as a Con too but considering the base idea this game tries to get everything out of the formula with excellent variation and details.  Sometimes you fly in space shooting things, sometimes you either fly in space or in a tunnel and try to avoid hitting things. And lets not forget the Boss fights.
Con's:
- Limited content in the end no matter what. This is one of those small games you pick and play and then put away. Forget about tens of hours of gameplay.
- Truly casual gamers with no will or skill to advance further will hit a wall relatively quick. Difficulty ramps up quite fast.

A city building sim that focuses on survival and management of settlers
WHATS THE GAME LIKE?
You manage your citizens' shelter, food, resources(tools,clothing,stone,wood), health and happiness. It is more in building stuff than ordering them around, like building a fishery to produce food, building a lumbermill to get wood for your woodcutter to produce firework for your houses for winter, and building a hospital to combat diseases. Basically you build stuff then watch them construct and operate the buildings. You watch as your little group grows to a 100 and more as years pass affecting your whole colony in their survival. The game also offers: managing the jobs and production of your citizens, item production (tools, clothing), trading, winter, and disasters. Like I said, It's different from other City builders since it has survival elements which if you fail to satisfy, its game over from starvation, hypothermia, disasters, and diseases.
PROS:
- Smart AI
- Great macromanagement (you are mostly laid back as your town grows)
- Simple and easy to understand
- Great season transitions with varying effects
- Challenging with a high possibility of losing if you mess up
- Various building choices (blacksmith, tailor, orchard, crops, mine, quarry, etc.)
- Mods
- Little to no bugs and glitches
CONS:
- Missing management tools (food/resource consumption control, multi/combined jobs, population control)
- No endgame stuff: mega buildings and decorations (the endgame is basically you filling the entire map with your town and surviving for years)
CONCLUSION
Highly recommended to buy if you're into City building/Management games with a challenge much like dwarf fortress. Its challenging and fun to play. it will definitly lead you to play it for hours to come.

is a roughly 4-hour long RPGMaker horror game. As such, it has inherent limitations, which it sometimes overcomes and sometimes falls prey to. It outdoes itself in terms of character design, mood, art and music, but falls short when it comes to game mechanics, pacing and a memorable story.
With that being said, what
outdoes itself in, many have outdone themselves in before it – and many will continue to do so after it. While this title may stand out among its RPGMaker siblings as pretty and plesant sounding, it is also the child that screams nonsense at the table over and over again when everyone is just trying to dine in peace.
doesn't understand when to elaborate its thoughts and when to show, rather than tell. Despite having eye-catching displays of its musings, it doesn't know
to voice them. An even bigger crime is that its silences come in packs, causing more discomfort than wonder.
Above of all, it doesn't understand that decent game mechanics should
exclude repeating the same tasks over and over again through unskippable cutscenes.
In short, while
succeeds in things that its genre isn't renowned for, it fails at a core aspect of good storytelling, be it a bedtime story or an intricate centuries-old tale: it fails at being memorable.
's biggest fault is being a niche game. It appeals to a specific kind of gamer and, if you're not lucky enough to find yourself in that category, its shortcomings will shine brighter than its gems. If, however, you find yourself inside the specific frame this game was painted for, its faults will hopefully simply be a speck of a drifting ship, lost in a sea of aesthetic graphics and darn good music.
I recommend
to seekers of good art and music, that enjoy their fair share of words, don't mind wonky puzzles and can handle some repetition. I don't recommend it to anyone that doesn't see themselves clearly in the previous sentence.

In many ways this game is the spiritual successor to the early Settlers games. It is peaceful to watch the citizens of the town move through their daily routines with no input from the player apart from nudges and course corrections. At any moment that can all disappear in a heartwrenching series of understated "dings." Lurking beneath that calm, almost hypnotic veneer is cruel fate that is ready to punish any miscalculation with harsh results. Namely the slow, almost unstoppable, death of the entire village.
I grew my first village too fast and ran out of food well before winter was over. As the population dwindled I found myself feeling slight pangs of guilt and heartbreak as the dings came and the graveyard filled. It was terrible, and the game provided no lifelines and gave no mercy. I was helpless.
That emotionless cruelty is matched by the games surprisingly idyllic and beautfiul landscapes. I was struck, often, at how delightful the game was to just watch. Many times I caught myself staring at the screen and enjoying the scenes as they unfolded. It is well executed.
There are some flaws of course. It does get repetitive (but really, what game doesn't?) and the tavern never seemed to work quite right for me. None of that takes away from the experience though. The fact that this game was almost entirely made by one programmer only deepens my respect for it.
If you like city building games, or games like Settlers II, I highly recommend this game!

-Unique Artwork. Creepy and cute are the only two words to describe it.
-Wonderful music to go along with the dark atmosphere.
-Puzzles. Challenging enough to make you think but not frustrating to the point of distracting from the story.
-I love the way the save feature was integrated into the game.
-Playtime is decent for the price.
-Game crashed for me quite frequently in the beginning. Not sure if a bug or isolated event.
-Default resolution is miniscule, making it full screen distorted it. Again, not sure if it’s just my PC and the way it was presented on my screen.
-Music is nice, but with that being said, it could get a bit repetitive when you're stuck on a puzzle.
-Accidently made dialogue choices by hitting enter too many times to make the text scroll faster.
Definitely worth the money if you're up for a decent story, interesting characters, incredible creepiness and a handful of jump scares.

Dont buy this game for more than a dollar. If you're expecting a fun space adventure like starfox or at least a fun shoot 'em up adventure like Panzer Dragoon, you're going to be dissapointed.
This game is functional, yes. It plays fine. However, its got bare minimum functionality. You shoot and move through space, occasionally getting power-ups. Don't ask what they do, the game doesnt tell you. How do you use them? You dont. They're auto applied to your ship and you lose them when you get hit.
Your ship (whichever of the three you chose, it wont really matter. They control slightly differently, but its not a major change) is always at the front of the screen and the camera scrolls you forward. enemies/obstacles pop up (and I mean pop up, its like it was made on the n64 the popup is so bad) so you can never tell where they're going to be. The field of view is incredibly small. There is a real lack of any substance. Yeah, you're in space shooting stuff, but it lacks all the things that made games like starfox cool
You dont see those squadrons of enemies approaching, battling in the background. Sometimes you're lucky if you get a planet background instead of black emptiness with the hyperspeed lines from starwars to indicate you're moving fast.
Boss battles arent anything special either. No cinematics, no sense of danger, no challenge. They just feel like regular enemies with health meters.
Also, there is no story in game. The game gives you about 0 feedback on anything that is going on. So, read up on the lore before playing, otherwise you'll be lost fighting the most uninspired aliens I've ever seen.
I think I played for 15 minutes. I dont think I'll pick it back up any time soon. Not really worth my play time, and chances are its not worth yours.
Its actually a port of a Wii ware game from 2009. So, dont expect anything of it at all. At 24 cents, I feel like I barely got what I payed for. There are flash games with more content.

Gameplay- 9.5/10
The gamplay is just fantastic and fun. There is a good variety of bosses, and the run and gun stages are very fun and hectic, too. The reason I didn't give it a solid 10 is because the game is about learning from your mistakes and playing the stage over and over until you perfect it. I myself like this type of difficulty, becuase the game forces you to git gud. You feel your skills improving, and i love that. Though, I understand the trial and error isn't for everybody, and might discourage some people.
Graphics- 15/10
Cuphead is easily one of the most unique and beautiful looking indie games that came out possibly ever. The 1940's Fleischer animation style is just filled to the brim with charm and creativity. The bosses and enemies are designed very creatively, and I can't wait for to see how the bosses will look later in the game. The graphics kept me smiling even after all those deaths I suffered. The game is so loyal to the style, that it really feels like you're playing through a cartoon straight from the 40's.
Sound- 11/10
The sound is equally as authentic and loyal to the era as the graphics are. The music is a lot of upbeat jazz that's just really nice to listen to. I especially love the title screen song. The sound effects are very 1940's-esque aswell. It's made by human mouths, and i just love it.
Difficulty and Fairness- 10/10
The difficulty is just excellent. The game doesn't hold your hand, but it's not ball-bustingly impossible, either. There is a lot of trial and error, but I like this because like i said before, the game forces you to improve and get better. Sure, you CAN buy items and weapons that'll make your life a little easier from the shop, but the game is still very much based on skill, not luck or items. This makes finally making it to the end of a level, or landing the final blow on a boss all the more satifiying, especially if you were struggling.
Overall 11/10
Cuphead is an excellent indie game that was completely worth the wait and delays. I implore you to buy this game if you're a fan of games like Contra or Mega man, if you're a fan of animation, or even if you're just curious. Cuphead is a gem that's worth every penny, and I'm eagerly waiting to see what StudioMDHR has in store next.

None of the answers were completely bizarre and I felt a sense of accomplishment when I figured the puzzles out, rather than relief like some games.
The art style is wonderful. The artist does care about the detail in the images and while anatomy might not be the strongest aspect at this point, the little things added in make all the difference and make the pictures fun.
I do think that perhaps a puzzle or two could be added at the start, since that felt very much more like a death trap at every turn as can pose a bit of an issue to get people into the game. Additionally there are more sounds that could stand to be added to the game, but for a free game I really got quite a bit.
In the end, it was a fun little game that changed from frustrating into rewarding and is a nice, quick game to play. Especially as we head towards Halloween.

Let me start off by saying this game is gorgeous. The black-and-white color scheme is visually striking, dark and beautiful. The sound effects are amazing, bringing to life the silhouetted events on screen.
And that's the problem.
The game starts simply, with basically two controls: movement and interact (take hold of an object and move it). I'm not typically a platform gamer, but this game handles smoothly and is more puzzley than platformery, which made my brief stint in LIMBO an overall enjoyable experience.
You play as a bright-eyed little boy, making his way from left to right through this the lonely landscape. The quiet ambiance is beautiful... until suddenly SNAP! He's caught in a trap, beheaded, blood spraying everywhere! As suddenly as it happened, it's over. The boy's body gently comes to rest on the ground, the silence broken only by the player's quiet weeping as you literally watch the light in the boy's eyes go out.
It's quite amazing, if a bit gruesome. Each mode of death has a different animation and perfectly corresponding sound effect. In the short time I played this game, my poor little character was: thrown off a cliff and got broken legs, impaled by spikes, drowned, dismembered by a bear trap, and squashed flat by a boulder. I was morbidly fascinated by how graphic the game was without really showing anything.
I made it up to the first big fight, where you battle a giant spider. You have to dodge away from the spider in order to obtain puzzle items needed to finish the fight. I was unable to make it through this fight. I started getting decent at watching the visual cues for when the spider was about to attack, but when it did, the sudden sound of its strike was too much for me. I grew more and more queasy every time my character was suddenly and horribly impaled, then shaken off to land in a crumpled heap on the ground.
This game is amazing to look at. You might like it, but know what you're getting into.

So far I've found it pretty engaging, although it does have some fairly serious bugs to work out (graphics glitches, Failure to load, indestructable bases, AI not being able to find capture points on some maps).  Given the Greenlight status, hopefully these will be ironed out in the near future, and once the correct voice packs have been added.  And it's also very nice to see a mod of any sort that focuses on the longest and one of the least represented conflicts of the 1930s/1940s.
The concept is great, and the feel of the forces is unique despite being obviously based on the US and German factions of the core game.  The specialisation trees add some interesting tricks and flavour to the two factions currently available (Imperial Japanese Army and Chinese Nationalist Resistance Army), and the detailing on both the maps and the models is exceptional.
In the future it would seem that this mod could also be a good launching point for Pacific content, Such as US marines or British Chindits (given how the unit balance has evolved, it would not seem viable to port over the existing European army lists, too much heavy armour).  Maybe even ANZAC troops (probably as a specialisation of the British) and some jungle/ island maps.
To summerise, this is an ambitious and interesting mod, a little unpolished but with a lot of promise.  I expect it will come into it's own as work is done on it, but be aware that as it stand it's still a work in progress.

For most of the people playing this game, the battle system will make little to zero sense.  The numbers you see on the screen are totals per combo, the final number being the amount of HP deducted from the thing you are fighting.
I finished the game at level 52, my heroes were initating attacks for about 50-80 dmg, with final combo damage of around 1500.
The story is interesting, it's almost like watching an anime or cartoon series and seeing how the protagonist evolves and matures as he develops skills and meets new people.  The problem is that the battles are so boring, I ended up binding turbos to Artes keys (B and A) using my Steam Controller and just holding them down during fights.  Sure you can exploit weaknesses, but it's not really necessary to finish the game.
The fast travel system is convoluted, you can't fast travel everywhere and sometimes it is greyed out to lock you into a cut scene when you enter a region.
Some of the boss mechanics aren't explained, I ended up fighting the final boss 3 times before realizing there's a trick to it.
Ultimately, this game is kind of a chore to slog through, wouldn't recommend it to fans of RPGs as it's more button mashing than strategizing attacks.

I first learned this mod existed a few months ago while looking through screenshots for CoH and decided to give it a try. Other than a few hiccups, it ran perfectly fine and I put more than a few hours into it.
Then I saw the announcement that it was going to Greenlight. Needless to say, I was extremely excited at the idea of having it on Steam for ease of updating and playability.
Anyway, let's get to the review:
PROS:
-A glimpse of a very-little represented aspect of the Second World War
-EXTREMELY detailed models and textures (seriously, on some rifles, it's possible to even see the arsenal marks)
-The battles can get absolutely BRUTAL, even by modded CoH standards
-Seemingly improved AI (expect serious challenges, especially on higher difficulties)
-Integrated devmode (SP cheat version) option, if you're into that
-Matches the classic feeling of CoH, while also bringing a fresh new experience to the table
CONS:
-From a historical standpoint, a few units are a bit unbalanced, but these may be addressed at a later point
-There are a few bugs (such as the game crashing when armored vehicles fight one another, that's fixable though), but nothing too detracting
NEUTRAL:
-At the time of review, the voices are still the vanilla American and German, but they are working on implementing Chinese and Japanese voices
-No campaign, but as they've stated before, they'd need mappers
-Chinese armored donkey bombs are terrifying
All things considered, this is an extremely well-made and fun mod for (arguably) one of the best WWII RTS games ever made.
