Hiragana Battle is a helpful tool for learning Hiragana for the first time, in an interesting and engaging way. Unfortunately, it has plenty of shortcomings, but I think it's still a worthwhile pick-up if you're looking for something to spruce up your studying a bit.
The game introduces you to Hiragana characters in sets of 5 and then you go on to "fight" them in various locations. In order to deal damage to an enemy Hiragana, you just need to provide the correct sound that Hiragana corresponds to.
Pros:
- Decent RPG with most of the basic elements you would expect (equipment, stats and skills)
- A kinda decent story, which is a welcome surprise given the game's purpose and subject
- A few cool music pieces
- Good in-game lessons and study guides
- Some vocabulary and phrases besides Hiragana are also provided
Cons:
- Bugs : I had a memory leak occuring around every 30 minutes. Extremely annoying, game would crash. Couple that with the game not having an auto-save feature and you can lose several minutes of progress at a time. Save as often as you can.
- The game tries a bit too much to be an actual RPG which sometimes gets in the way of learning. Fall a bit behind in equipment or levels and you'll have trouble progressing, which can be annoying if you feel you've already learned the current set of Hiragana already. Thankfully it doesn't take too much to grind yourself back up to where you should be.
-  Another huge problem I had with the game is that the Hiragana that you fight were not really random and mixed-up. Each fight you get into is more or less against the same Hiragana in every region, making it very hard to learn all the Hiragana properly. As new Hiragana are introduced, you almost never fight any of the older ones, making it really easy to forget them. This should have been the best part of the game for learning and yet it's not there.
- Some Quality of Life improvements are really missing. Why is there no option to return to base immediately while in a dungeon?
Overall, it's an okay game but there's several improvements that could be made.

LIMBO is a cute, but dark 2-D game that utilizes clever little puzzles that includes the use of physics. There is no solid narrative or introduction, but the basis revolves around a boy in search of his sister at the "edge of Hell." The gameplay is solid, but the menu and settings are minimalistic which will lead you to editing the "settings.txt" file in order to change functions such as alternative key bindings and screen resolution. Most reviewers say that LIMBO is video game art and I would have to agree since it brings film noir-like effects including its monochromatic presentation, film grain and creepy atmospheric sounds. LIMBO is a quick, satisfying form of entertainment suitable to casual and Indie video game fans.

So, the following premises shall state my opinions about this freshly 2017 game. Graphics-wise, I have no problem, as I am used to top-down perspective, and I believe this game is crafted masterfully as the graphics have shown the feel the game supposed to show. With such graphics, even people with low-end personal computers and laptops can still engage in this game. In other words, I believe it is perfect fit, graphics-wise and player-wise! Another factor is the gameplay. I find it similar to Bloodline Champions (?, not sure about this. Haven't seen that game for a long time) and Battlerite, but the difference is that, abilities are used through swiping your mouse, which is a rare feature! Community-wise, I had no problems, as I don't see much players talking trash or whatnot, by the use of the in-game communication system or the global chat. The cons I see, so far, is that I don't see much players yet, though I'll overlook this for a while due to the age of the game. I don't know much about the population on the external client, but I hope the Steam community may consider playing this game as well. Good mechanics, acceptable graphics and unique gameplay: I definitely would recommend this game.
In addition, I would like to say thanks for the free Unnyworld Founder's Pack that I received. Awesome job!
That's all I could say, for now. Enjoy gaming!

This game is better balanced than the original dungeon defender's overall.  The way they're handling Free to Play is significantly annoying, but not at the same level of annoyance as Dungeon Defender's Eternia (aka Dungeon Defender's Can We Have Your Wallet).  Don't expect deep game play, this is a party game pure and simple, there's not a ton of complexity and as with the original, every hero is overpowered when you're playing to their strengths.  It's intended to be a "pick it up and just start playing it" sort of a game, versus a "if I don't put this tower in exactly this spot we're all going to die."
I see a number of reviews talking about being forced to play levels specific ways -- there are lanes, and you block the lanes.  That's inherent in tower defense.  Each character has their things that they can do to effectively block a lane, and so when you're playing you do have to play each lane the way that character does things.  If you are playing solo, usually there really is exactly one good way to play the level with a given character.  If you're playing team, usually there are multiple arrangements that work -- you can optimize, you can split up lane by lane, and you'll be succesful either way.
Again, low playtime on the PC version is because the Playstation 4 version plays better.
On the networking, early versions had a bug that if two devices were on the same LAN, the network game would fail consistently (e.g. if you had two computers).  That seemed to be corrected the last time we tried it, the Playstation version had the same bug.

Blood Bowl 2 is the mutant ofspring of american football and the fantassy warhammer world. The game is sertannly a great laugh but also is serious enough to justify long term dedicated game time.
This game inspires me to rage and ROFL in equal mesures depending on who nuffle ( blood bowl's god) shines on that day.

Bob and Jim our beloved ogre and vampire commentators never fail to make me laugh, a great example here (
)
The gameplay has 2 layers.
1.The first of witch is where you design and change your team to fit you need as you manage things like your teams money and how many chearleaders you want to have.
2. The second layer is the actual pitch where the game takes a TBS role where you posistion your players and fight all over the ball with the ultamate aim of scoreing more touchdowns than your rival.
PERFORMANCE
Has been outstanding for me to say the least next to no loading time and good frame rates throughout. (and i have been recoding gameplay on top so performance is awesome for me to say the least.
FOR PEOPLE NEW TO BLOOD BOWL ( Starting guide )
Orks and humans are the 2 teams id recomend starting with there good allrounders.
orks if you want to be more blocky (fighting / killing) and humans if you want better controll of the ball.
After you have a few games under our belt you may want to try a more specilised team with a playstyle you seem to lean towards and or like.
For example you try the Humans out but notice you like to bash in your rivals head ... well then try moveing on the the dwarfs or the orks if you dont want to give up the ball game alltogether :P
At first it may seem like you have nothing but bad luck with turnover after turnover and the game is treating you badly for some reason but a large part of the game is risk managment to reduce those turnover and a good coach knows how to manage those risks.
a few good tips for this are
1. Allways stand up your fallen players asap
2. Prioritse low risk and high reward actions before the vice versa
FOR BLOOD BOWL VETRANS / CHANGES FROM BB1
Its the old game you loved with a few ballance changes such as the ork blitzer has increased in price. ( I would go into more detail but as its the beta i expect they will either revert back or change more after the release / in updates to come)

AI

My probelm with this game is that in every way it is not worth $30. I put in about $5 when it was in kickstarter and it's totally worth that but anyone who paid $30 got ripped. They will never finish this game, it was their toy, and now that they have made some money on what is now an outdated game, they will do what they have done with other games and move on. It's a shame, but it's true.
HOWEVER, this game could be a ton of fun with very little work involved. make the game as-is right now but add the ability to download from a third party, cars and tracks and for gods sake fix the damn MP to function. Every time i join a race I'm all psyched thinking "i have a ping of 50 this race should be incredible" only to be disappointed when the screen constantly flutters and my car jumps around on the track and i have momentary loss of all control over the car for a half second at a time.
Even more idiotic is the control scheme. they have (what i can only imagine) is gear selections for someone with an H shifter (6 gears+ reverse) however, there is no clutch binding, rendering that useless, and if you go with some sort of sequential, you might as well just select automatic, because the shifts are so slow I could complete a lap around one of the Oval tracks before someone could shift from reverse to 5th gear and back... just kinda sad. it's like grandma is sitting in the passenger seat trying to shift the gears for you. There is no real support for axis controls. The throttle only really gets recognized at about 50% anything before that makes the engine do funny stuff like not work or sputter or just go full throttle, the steering axis seems to be the only one that works, and I'm pretty sure if you set an axis for handbrake it doesn't work at all. All of which the axis cannot be calibrated. This goes for any controller, xbox controller, wheel, doesn't matter, it just doesn't work well.
Lastly, The soft body physics were supposed to be the spotlight of the game yet they are an embarassment to anyone in the animations world because it's so terrible and fake. The cars deform, but not realistically. Watch some video's of Beam.NG that is true car deformation. This game should have that, but instead it is as if your car is build from some kind of metal that after it gets hit with "x" amount of force it turns into putty and then back hard. It's laughable, and somwhat comical at times, but to be honest I would rather the frame break or a wheel fall off than to have some warped up car with two wheels still able to drive at full speed even though the engine is bent at a 45° angle and would not function any longer. Yes it's supposed to be a goofy game, but how goofy do we really want it to be?
That brings up another point. The devs brag about a tire model to make it realistic yet show no concern to make the game realistic. I think the devs got lost somewhere and didn't know what to do, and to be honest I think it was when they started selling the game. I think they said "heck with making what we started, let's just conform to our target market" and that tarket market is somewhere between chimps on cocaine and Sim racers looking to goof off, which would actually be a great discription of how this game is made. Some parts are super awesome, other parts seem to have came out of a coloring book.
I'm just not sure what this game is or isn't supposed to be and every time you go to mention an issue with the game on any forum, you will be blasted for questioning it. I don't see how so many people can drink the kool-aid thinking this game will be finished when it took nearly a year for a single update to drop on this game. Let's face it a year between updates means they don't care anymore, regardless of what they post on their website.

My First Impressions Video:
Old school 3D graphics with the ability to move both horizontally side to side and vertically as well.
The game is pretty fun with different levels each changing up the targets and obstacles on screen, everything from asteriods to big spiked indesuctible metal balls to enemy ships.
Pros:
- Acceptable 3D old school sprite style graphics
- Movement is responsive and fast paced
- Dodging the oncoming asteroids and ships is actually fun
- Blowing stuff up, despite the lackluster explosions is satisfying
- levels change it up each time you advance, so you're always doing something a little different from the last level
Cons:
- No 360 twin stick controller support (at the time of this review but a developer has said such support is planned)
- No score to be seen while playing the levels (Even though it adds up your score at the end of each level, the score could still be kept during the gameplay, and an assessment of the score at the level end could be done and then player could recieve a bonus is applicable)
- No real power ups or ability to "skill up" your ship to move faster, shoot faster etc that I saw
- defeating enemies and blowing up asteroids is wayyy too basic and lackluster.  Big explosions would be very nice in a game like this, especially in the year 2015, not seeing more satisfying explosions is disappointing
Overall, this game is easily worth it's asking price of $3.99 USD and certainly it's sale price.  While you likely won't be spending dozens of hours in this game, if you get an hour or two of fun out of it total over the next month or two, then it's more then worth the price tag.
Advice: I would wait until the support is added for a twin stick controller (Xbox 360 controller support) especially if you enjoy playing games like this with a controller over a keyboard.
My Rating:  65% out of 100 (But this rating is moved up to a 75% considering its low price tag)

My first Long Dark Experience:
I played through this sandbox mode a few different times on hard. I wasn't too used to it yet and kept losing at life early in the game, so I decided to try the easiest mode where I figured I could survive for longer than 24 hours to get a real understanding of the game. Just after spawning I stumbled upon a Logging Campsite where I found a few essential items like pop and canned food, as well as newspapers and firewood. After warming up and resting for a while I left with every intention of finding high ground to see if I could see any other man made structures I could venture off to. High ground was reached where I saw something that looked like a cabin sitting on the top of a mountain in the distance. I made it over there in just ten minutes or so of running, It was a lot closer than It looked. At the base of the hill the cabin was sitting on, I sprained my ankle so I was slightly immobilized and had to walk rather than sprint to the top. At this time I thought freezing to death would be a problem. Luckily for me, it wasn't. I made it to the top where I found a hunting rifle with 5 rounds, plus some more essentials like food, and firewood. I rested until 7:30 the next morning. My ankle felt better so I ran down the mountain, shot a deer and a wolf. I skinned, gutted, and then I took the meat. I made a small fire, accidentaly burned myself, and then ate. At this point I ran further and found some train tracks. I followed them and found a frozen lake with little fishing shacks on it and a cabin on the shoreline. I went inside the closest building which was the cabin, where I started a fire, crafted a snare, line, hook, and a few more items at the workbench. Then I went upstairs, where I searched a dead body and found a candy bar, started a fire, and went to bed. I died in my sleep of dysentery... That burn I recieved when I made the fire became infected because It wasn't properly treated. All I had in my medical kit was a bandage, which was useful but I also needed antibiotics. Of course I did not have any... Little did I know I had Inflammation of my Intestines accompanied by bloody diarrhea. What a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ way to die... Over all, the gameplay is excellent. I like the non-realistic look to the game and everything you have to accomplish to survive. Only complaint, is that it doesn't have multiplayer.
11/10 Would get dysentery again.

Banished is possibly the most challenging city sim. That i have ever played. The game is extremely punishing to those who go in there thinking "Oh it's just like Sim City" lol. No, it isn't. This game is very detailed in almost every aspect to how your town is from the overall health of your citizens, happiness, and, how many jobs are there avaiable as well as citizens.
I mean seriously this game has a graph to keep track of progress of every little thing from resources, to population, to supplies. This game is very well informative. Plus the tutorials are also a big help. The developers really put a lot of hard work into the game. Just make sure you keep your citizens happy and use critical thinking skills in applying to the needs of your citizens and you should be fine :)
Plus this game has a modding community behind it. To make the game better or slightly easier for newcomers to the game.
The only downside to this game is the overall "disasters" In this game it's either natural (tornadoes, fires) or medicial (diseases, and such). With that being said, The game doesn't have any bandits, wolf attacks, or neighboring towns for you to take over. Lol, yes i know what your thinking "But um this is a building city simulation. Not some sort of RTS conquest" and yes i get that. However the disasters happen rarely. Sometimes not at all. This game is a great time killer. But that is actually the problem. Lol, i want to be more active with my village. Maybe trade it with other villages that I have created, or defending my town from bandits and wolves, or take over other towns that are randomly generated on the map. Perphaps share the world space with a friend who has the game as well?
If the developers are going to make a second Banished game. I sincerely hope they add more "disasters" in the game. It's a great start, plus the game overall should keep you busy. Not everyone will like this game because of these elements or lack of certain elements. But hey who knows maybe a modder will make something like this in the near future? So don't get your hopes up
All and all. If you like delicate city building simulations. This game is for you.

This game is exactly the kind of horror game that I like - not too long, mostly story and atmosphere oreinted, with minimal jumpscares. Seriously, I hate jumpscares, but their infrequent enough in this game that I still really enjoyed it. This game is dark, unsettling, and scary at times, but it is far from your typical hardcore game. For those looking for a true thrill, this is not a game for you. If you're looking for what is basically a "point-and-click" adventure with a horror theme and super dark atmosphere, then I recomend checking this game out. This is not ACTUALLY a point and click - you control your character with the arrow keys and interact by pressing a button on the keyboard (I forgot which one, but that's not important) - but the puzzles in this game operate very similarly.  You explore, find clues and itmes, and use the clues to figure out what to do with the items. Most of the puzzles in this game are quite good, although there are a couple less-than-superb ones as well that are either frustrating or tedious. There is no combat, so the exploration and puzzles make up 100% of the gameplay, but the biggest attraction is the story and atmosphere.
The story is wonderful. The game is one big metaphorical mystery that all ties together at the end, and I quite enjoyed it. This game absolutely worth playing just for the story. It's not too long (about 2-3 hours), so there's no excuse not to find time to experience this atmospheric horror story game. Highly recomended for anyone who likes dark short stories and doesn't mind puzzles.

A small touch on the item system. Many players complain that item system is too difficult for understand, however note that between this game and other games. The relationship of stats and skills are inverse. So typically most RPG games follow sequence where your next set of gear is usually better than last set, however this game put more enphase on the type of skills on your equipment rather then raw stat values and this concept is reversed in berseria. For this reason, Many people drop the game for its complexity, but if you take the time to understand the drop & fusion system, You may find yourself enjoying this game more then you previous gave it credit for.

The game does a fairly okay job at introducing the player to each hiragana character, though with some problems.
It introduces the characters in sets, showing each one to the player and providing the sound and how the character would be written on paper. This would be fine, if it were not for the very poor choices in fonts which don't even remain consistent in the game, switching between caligraphy styles and more web-safe fonts.
Other than that, having to 'kill' each character repeatedly over the course of the game is a solid way of giving the player the chance to memorize each character's associated sound. The game also provides minor side lessons on actual words which help show how the characters would sound when pronounced together.
This is where everything falls apart. You have to REALLY enjoy retro JRPGs to wade through this incredible mess.
The game is blatantly a very poor RPG maker product, including all the out of the box issues with no added quality of life enhancements.
Moving around is a pain, everything looks bad visually, battles are incredibly tedious and frustrating, the game demands you grind for levels, and worst of all: Featureless maze based dungeons.
The issues
presents as a game, seriously hinder the quality as a learning tool. The point of a learning game is to make learning interesting and fun, and this game did not do it. Battles were the main flaw, though wandering through empty mazes  while being battered with random encounters helped bring everything down.
The idea of the battles was fine. Fight hiragana characters by attacking them with the matching sounds. This was a good idea. The issue a culmination of having a long list of sounds to search through everytime you want to hit something, not being able to click directly on the character once you have the selected sound, then having to do this for each member of your party even if there's not enough characters to go around, possibly multiple times during the battle if you're not strong enough to kill the characters in one hit,  and then waiting for the battle to play out.
It would have worked much better if each fight was always 4 characters lined up, one for each party member, selecting the sounds for each, and then having it all go down at once with one-hit kills. Incorrect selections would of course result in party members taking damage, and any surviving characters would need to be attacked again,
.
Hell, even a fast forward button for combat might have made it a less mind-numbing experience.

Clean and distinct. More lights here and there wouldn't harm, if the hammer of the gods goes all over the place again (no pun intended), destroying light sources.
The music is GOLD and the controls are fluid, which is a must for this type of game - and the devs pulled them off real nice. Playing it with mouse/kb or gamepad feels both equal, but i prefer the gamepad to have all functions within the reach of my thumb.
Basically you clear a level and descent deeper into the dungeon. You can find different weapons that really make a difference to your gameplay. Unfortunately the game feels unfinished and you will encounter bugs (falling through the floor, levetating) or run out of things to explore pretty fast.
If you like Gauntlet/Crimsonland/Hotline Miami 1 and brawlers in general, you might give it a try despite my negative review. Just don't set your expectations high.

Genre: Action/Indie/Early Access
Release Date: 17 Jul, 2015
Completionist Gameplay: Endless
Barbara-ian is a top-down run and gun action game with a female protagonist. This should already make you want to play the game. If you need further convincing, read on.
With only one hit point standing between you and certain death (and the loss of your beloved Tome of Laser Vision), Barbara-ian is the true definition of exciting. If you liked Hotline Miami, I would absolutely recommend buying this. The game being in Early Access shouldn’t deter you. Barbara-ian is fully playable and is not missing any key components. The only reason it is still in Early Access is because the developers want to continue adding more content for us to enjoy.
One of my favourite parts about this game is how it forces you to diversify your strategies and step out of your comfort zone. Each time you generate a dungeon will not be like the last, and after many hours of playing I don’t think I remember seeing the same layout twice.(If there was, it was because I died so often I didn’t get a chance to properly remember). To progress, you must unlock multiple chests each level. These chests include weapons that make the enemies you will face slightly easier to kill. You don’t get a choice about which weapons you unlock, so learning how to use them efficiently and without blowing yourself up is a must, and you’ll need to learn quickly. There are holes in the floor that lead to lava and acid and you have the choice of avoiding them completely or using them as traps, luring in your enemies, hoping that they’ll fall in. You’ll be surprised by a swinging sword or a mass of goblins hidden away in a dark corner of the dungeon, or you’ll accidentally knock your only light source to the other side of the room. The entire game forces you to think strategically on your feet, while also testing your reaction time, control and nerves.
I also love the physics of this game. When you die, which will be often, you get to watch Barbara fling away across the map, or crumple into a ball. It’s very entertaining to watch, and definitely a smart idea when you think about how often you’ll be dying in this game.
Barbara-ian as a whole has managed to find the perfect balance between having a character who feels weighty and real, while also managing to incorporate the feeling of incredibly smooth movement. You can play with both a controller and a keyboard, and after trying both I can honestly say that both feel just as easy to learn and as natural as the other.
Just like Hotline Miami, Barbara-ian’s soundtrack is catchy and never gets old. The title screen song is gold, and you’ll be singing it to yourself in the shower and on the bus. There are in-game controls for both the music and the actual sound effects of the game, and while they are a little fiddly, they work perfectly and are easy to find.
What caught my eye first about this game was how hilarious the trailer was. After playing Barbara-ian, not only have I not been disappointed, I can’t wait until I can play more. Use it as a stress relief or the new flappy-bird, either way, I can definitely see this becoming one of the more popular games on the steam store.

Tales of Zestiria is pretty good - the length is right and the combat is fun. Like other tales games it's an action rpg but you will find yourself stopping mid-battle to manage recovery items and the sort. There are some options in terms of the types of attacks your characters peform, too, but it doesn't stray far from the hero being the sword guy, the girl being a caster and so on.
The plot is a bit slow to develop and it's pretty standard fare -- good guy with a mysterious past must defeat all evil and restore the world type stuff. Things get a lot more interesting after the first ten hours or so - with subquests to do all around the various towns.
The game runs pretty well on a modern rig - an i5 6500 w/ a GTX 1070 was able to run it at 60 fps maxed most of the time (you'll need the TOZfix patch to unlock the 30fps limiter bamco has on the game). It's not a bad entry if you're looking to get into the Tales series.

Cuphead is a
perfect game.  Gorgeous, highly creative art, amazing soundtrack, easy to pick up but hard as nails to complete...it's one of the best games I've played this year.  It's absolutely infuriating at times, but no moreso than the retro games it's inspired by, and all your failures just make your successes all the more powerful.
Every time I thought "THIS IS IMPOSSIBLE" I tried and tried again until I could feel the rhythm of each level, learning to play the controller like a musical instrument.  When I finally completed the last boss, I stood up, threw my fists straight up in the air, and gave a euphoric, triumphant "
".  What a game.  And all this for a measly 20 bucks.
If I
to make one critique?  The overworld could have been more interesting.  It was mostly static with NPCs that weren't very memorable.  Nothing really to do in it, with few secrets to be found.  It mostly just served as a means to select your level, but it could have been more.  It could have had some mini activities to give you a little downtime and change up the pace before you rushed headfirst into the next punishing level.
That's pretty much it.
There have been a hell of a lot of great titles this year, but I hope Cuphead receives all the awards it deserves.  It is a masterpiece in its genre and will be enjoyed for many years to come.

Fantastic introductory "course" with a significant focus on learning, I recommend combining it with other learning tools. Personally I took the Hiragana courses in the Duolingo app while playing the game.
Don't expect too much depth from the RPG side of the game, it's very simplistic and the most effective strategy will often boil down to kill - kill - kill. It's also easy to get significantly ahead of the power curve, allowing all of your characters to always go first and one shot most enemies until very late in the game.
That said, if you're here you probably care more about what the game offers in terms of learning, and it offers quite a lot. If you follow the games' instructions, not only will you get some great knowledge of Hiragana, very basic vocabulary and grammar, but you'll also end up with your own Hiragana guide, with some vocabulary sprinkled on top.
The game takes about 10-12 hours to 100 %, depending on how much time you spend in the learning sessions, and whether or not you grind experience.
Finally I just want to add that the game will seem very easy initially, but rest assured, if you have no knowledge of japanese and hiragana, there'll be plenty of challenge in the game if you just keep at it.

Very creative teaching mechanism that works quite well! If I had to crunch down on papers and paragraphs of strictly academic learning, there's no telling how much I'd lose focus and how much more drained I would feel after studying.
Throw in characters, gameplay, sidequests, and buying new weapons and armor, and things are suddenly more interesting. Grinding to level up doesn't feel like grinding, it feels like studying.
After 10 hours of gameplay, 9 of which is actual studying, I've got most hiragana memorized. Due to the fact some are more memorable than others coupled with the fact that some appear in the game more often than others, there are a small amount that take me a few more moments to remember.
In any case, I'm very impressed with how effectively this game taught me. It probably helped me that I took two years of Japanese in high school some years ago, but by now I had completely forgotten most hiragana.
I definitely recommend this if you want to learn hiragana in a fun and interesting way!

Never have I see a game that utilizes time as a mechanic to such degree; you are the master of every situation because the enemy depends on your movement. SUPERHOT is not for those who are looking forward to an adventurous storyline, since there isn't much. But if you are dying for a fresh new take on the fps genre, then SUPERHOT well worth the price. And if you are willing to buy a brilliant piece of virtual artwork, then SUPERHOT considered relatively "cheap" amongst other artworks. It's the most innovative shooter I've played in years.

Short story, point-and-click type of adventure with a rather dark and slightly twisted Choose Your Adventure style presentation.  Most paths will kill you, and the words, "Your adventure ends here," will become writ in stone before you find certain clues that guide positive progress.
For those who seek achievements, there is a fantastic guide that will get you through the game in about 35 minutes (my estimation, based on choices that took me a bit to re-figure after "ending my adventure here" so often).
For an indie game from an unknown dev, this is an easy, easy thumb up to Brad Moore, and for a point & click game, I rate it thumb up as well.  While it's not animated and glittery, it's one of those honest little games that fills a niche for storytelling fans and those looking for an interesting diversion.
Finally, seeing what the achievements are really for was amusing in the manner of, "OMG I can die *that* way, too??"
Props, Brad - this is a nice diversion at a bargain price.

UnnyWorld? More like Un-interesting!
The premise is simple yet complicated so allow me to bring you upto speed very quickly with this one.
The game features two modes of which the first is traditional MOBA style gameplay where you destroy towers and creeps in a 3v3 symmetrical arena and win or lose when the base is destroyed.
the second mode is your clash of clans clone where you build up a homeworld and repel invaders and invade other players.
Both of these suck for different reasons and while I actually like the merging of the two ideas the execution is just dumb.
The first problem is that the MOBA aspect is dumbed down so you don't buy items from a store, you don't go jungling or taking center lane (there is no center lane!) you don't do anything you would traditionally expect from a MOBA to be blunt. This would be okay since the game is aimed at a very young audience and might even be an entry level MOBA except that the experience is so shallow (due to removing all depth to simplify the game) that you will see everything and do everything in a match after a single play, no exaggeration!
So we go to the clash of clans aspect and lets just get this out of the way immediately, you cannot delete or move structures, period. If you make a mistake (and you will) then its tough luck buddy and you are stuck with it. In games like this where you need to build a fantastic maze structure to prevent invaders, being restricted in this way is frankly unforgivable since any major mistake requires re-rolling your whole account! I have never even heard of such short sightedness! Also as is the norm for these types of games you require building A to unlock building B or for them to be certain levels but the game never tells you what buildings are required so you scratch your head wondering why you can't do things!
Finally the game is a mobile port and it shows, oh does it show. You play on little super mario galaxy planets which on a touchscreen would be easy to spin around but not so much on PC. It also has all the trappings of a mobile game and 3 currencies where only 1 really matters and on this note there is one thing that really ticked me off!
Unnycoins. They are not the premium currency but you can ONLY get them from being in a guild. Dead game is dead because of course it is so how do I set up my own guild? by spending over $1000 on in game currency! Are you mad?! Unnycoins are mostly worthless but I can't get this fake currency without splashing out on the real currency (Diamonds)! No wonder the population is so low!
I don't know what the team behind this were thinking if they were even thinking at all. I assume they assumed the mobile market was just easy money for no effort and when that didn't pan out they decided steam would be easy money.
I would say play it once, you really only
to play it once to see everything it offers anyway so its not like you miss out either way.
After playing some more since my initial first impressions I am a bit more forgiving of the game but I still can't recommend it. Firstly you can move structures you simply click on it then drag it where you want to move it too. This is unintuitive since clicking on a building brings up a menu so you wouldn't think to just drag the thing! I only discovered this by mistake which is a bad sign! Secondly Unnycoins are obtained by being in a party, not a guild.
You get 1 unnycoin per victory per party member excluding yourself so that means 2 Unnycoins per victory with each match being between 3 to 5 minutes. The things you can BUY with Unnycoins are not cheap such as a Heroes which cost 100 UC minimum and scaling up to 500. That means 250 victories just to unlock one hero at the high end of the spectrum and ONLY in a party. If we got 1 UC and upto 3 in a party I could forgive it but as is its just a stupid bottle neck.
Thankfully you can buy characters with real money but for some stupid reason you can't buy UC. Why is that an issue? Because you need UC to upgrade your spells which is just as important if not more so, than the heroes themselves.
I apprechiate the fast pace of the game but the game really has a long way to go before it is acceptable.

This game may look simple, with its 2D platforming stylistics and its apparent lack of a storyline, high definition graphics and bright neon colours. But make no mistake, Limbo is not simple at all. The simplistic design, smart use of sounds and greyscale filling complements with the complex mind-baffling story lying therin within the sleek elements of the game. What gripped me was how the story was told, not by words or flashbacks like most games, but within the action of the main character itself and your imagination. Why am I here? Who am I? Why is this here and why is that there?
Limbo brings you to a place to deep and dark that your only friend is the wordless little boy whom you are controlling. Unforgiving obstacles that sometimes culminates in morbid irony, leaving me speechless while I watch my own undoing. One can only marvel at the intricate design the developers have so carefully designed and enacted in the environment that is limbo. The whole world becomes dark and cold, a depressing stench hangs in the air, enveloping your mind and leaving you wanting more.
Like most puzzle games, you will get a sense of achievement when you have successfully solved a puzzle, but Limbo takes it one step further by giving you no rest after solving an obstacle. Have you cleared an obstacle? Good job, here is another one tumbling towards you and it will crush you in 3, 2, 1, splat. You're dead, and you restart.
Limbo is for both the casual and the hardcore gamer. When you step into this world, sit back and enjoy the ride, watching this lonely place unfurl before your eyes.
Take heed, however, this isn't for the faint of heart (or those who gets easily frustrated when stuck for ages). Also, should you play Limbo, do yourself a favour and do not look for video walkthroughs during your first playthrough. Experience the game fully at least once before going back again for the collectibles and achievements!
Definitely worth the 10 dollars, even more so when it is on sale. 9/10.

BioShock isn't a "shooter" in the conventional sense. Yes there are guns and crazed enemies and wild locales, but this game is so, so much more than your average sci-fi CoD.
Without going into too much detail, this game successfully blends story driven gameplay and choices with absolutely stellar level design and first person exploration/combat. BioShock is set in the vivid, stunningly realized underwater world of Rapture, filled to the (literally) bursting point with political intrigue, emotional decisions, stellar (voice) acting and so much more.
On the combat side of things, it's geared greatly towards the thinking man, offering a huge plethora of upgrade options, gameplay mechanics and some very unique and interesting abilities. All this would've been much less enjoyable had the AI been neglected, but thankfully the splicers, as they are known, are reasonably intelligent and display some interesting manuvers while fighting.
I must cut this short; I could ramble on for a good while about this game. I cannot recommend this highly enough. The sheer sense of "wow, this truly feels like a place that once existed" is off the charts. The combat is addictive. The story is one of the most unique offerings I've seen in videogames, especially the villain. Get this. Especially for one of the frequent bundles with BioShock 2 (also well worth getting, though not quite as stellar) this is just so worth your time.

Like others who had originally paid for this game, I feel a little slighted by the shift to the Microtransaction model. Being "rewarded" with a single title and a small amount on abstracted in-game currency feels like a bit of a betrayal. I realise I backed a game that was not released and that was my fault entirely. Just had slightly higher hopes from TrendyEnt than what was received.
PROS:
-Its basically just updated Dungeon Defenders
-Controls are responsive, if a slight departure from the original game. Vetrans to DD may find it awkward that all towers must be walked to and pointed at to be intereacted with, as opposed to just going into an aerial m view and selecting everything, Placing towers also feels wonky without this.
-All the characters from the original have made a return (or are in the works) with more to come. That said, they're a grind to unlock regularly, or you can opt to pay a microtransaction.
There suppose to (maybe) still be a PvP MOBA-style game mode with a large selection of classes to chose from. This might be worth checking out eventually.
CONS:
-I feel the new tarvern is too large, anjd awkwardly spaced. This is entirely personal.
-The community seems to be kinda eh. I can remember jumping into the old one with a bunch of randos and co-ordinating builders and repairment and whatnot, all without a hitch. This time around everyone seems to do their own thing
-The mana handed out at the begining of a way is untrue to the previous game. Now each player can open exactly one chest. Mana can still be given to other players, but this makes having one builder difficult, especially given the tone of the community.
-The inventory and hero deck function essentially makes the Defender's Forge obsolete, yet it still remains, I'm assuming only because a team member spent time modlling, rigging, and animating it.
-The bag system is abysmal - if I have 10 bags, why do they all have to be in the same window? Why not allow players to have multiple bag windows so as to not force you to constanly open and close them and drag and drop and scroll etc.
-Early Access and still microtransactions. This is another personal point, but I feel that Steam should disallow any game that is tagged as "Early Access" from having a microtransaction store.
-To me, maps feel awkward and sprawling, even if they do have a good flow, especially the early levels when compared to those of the first game. Perhaps sightlines could be improved
-Its hard to convince friends to play this F2P game. This could just be my personal circle of friends, but most are more willing to play DD1 and start everything fresh there than they are to do anything here.
-Personally, I prefer the old art direction largly over the one this game presents
Overall, the game isn't terrible, but it has shifted its direction and that's kinda left a bad taste in my mouth. I wouldn't say to strictly avoid this game, but would agree that this is a game you can skip and not have missed anything.
